chunks: Ahmad narrated from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa al-Kilabi who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) the first: 'Ali ibn Shihaab complains of his head, and the cold is severe, and he intends to enter the state of Ihram.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If it is as you claim, let him shade himself. And as for you, brightness (or clarity) is for the One for whom you are wearing Ihram.'

key_terms.أَحْرَمْتَ: You are wearing Ihram / You have entered Ihram
key_terms.إحرام: Ihram, the state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim in Ihram who needs to shade themselves due to headache or cold?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the permissibility of shading the head for a pilgrim suffering from a headache or cold, distinguishing between the physical relief and the spiritual state of Ihram. The phrase 'brightness is for the One' (or 'illumination belongs to God') underscores that the act of seeking relief does not invalidate the sacred state, as the pilgrim remains in a state of devotion. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on ease (*taysir*) within ritual obligations, ensuring that physical ailments do not become undue burdens during Hajj.

en.hubeali: Ahmad, from Usman Bin Isa Al Kilaby who said,

‘I said to Abu Al-Hassanasws the 1st that Ali Bin Shihaab complained about his headache and the intense cold, and he intends to wear Ihraam. So heasws said: ‘If it was as you are claiming, so let him shade (himself). And as for you, so brightness is for the Oneazwj Whom you are wearing Ihraam for’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ahmad has narrated from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa al-Kilabiy who has said the following:

“I once said to abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that Ali ibn Shihab has a headache, and cold is severe and he wants to assume the state of Ihram. He (the Imam) said, ‘If that is the case he can use shadows, but you must stay out of the shadow for the sake of the One for whom you assume the state of Ihram.’”
